## (d) Extrapolation: trajectory and predicted next moves

1. **2016–2018: Breaking defenses.** "Defensive Distillation is Not Robust to Adversarial Examples"; "Adversarial Examples Are Not Easily Detected." Advice codifying evaluation: 
  > "a defense is only interesting from the perspective of a security evaluation if it withstands future attack. Showing that a defense can defeat previous attacks is a necessary, but not sufficient, component of an evaluation."  
  > -- `research__advice_on_evaluating_adversarial_example_defenses_f3b3c399` (2018-05-26; solo author) 
  > "it is not these papers, and these papers only, that were performing weak evaluations. The field as a whole is. These recommendations come from approaches I notice that we were taking that others were (are) not."  
  > -- `research__advice_on_evaluating_adversarial_example_defenses_f3b3c399` (2018-05-26; solo author)
2. **2019–2020: Evaluation methodology and adaptive attacks.** "On Evaluating Adversarial Robustness"; "On Adaptive Attacks to Adversarial Example Defenses." 
  > "Defending against non-adaptive attacks is necessary but not sufficient. It is our firm belief that an evaluation against non-adaptive attacks is of very limited utility."  
  > -- `research__on_evaluating_adversarial_robustness_b187c740` (2019-02-18; first author) 
  > "Adversarial robustness is a negative goal – for a defense to be truly effective, one needs to show that no attack can bypass it."  
  > -- `research__on_evaluating_adversarial_robustness_b187c740` (2019-02-18; first author)
3. **2020–2023: Privacy, memorization, extraction, poisoning.** "Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models"; "Membership Inference Attacks From First Principles." 
  > "The paper I eventually wrote argued the field should use a much simpler approach---treating membership inference as the hypothesis test it actually is---and evaluate using a different metric. A few years on, that's what everyone does."  
  > -- `research__how_to_win_a_best_paper_award_or_an_opinionated_ta_54221651` (2026-03-09; solo author)
4. **2022–2023: Test-validity tooling and LLM alignment robustness.** "Increasing Confidence in Adversarial Robustness Evaluations"; "Are aligned neural networks adversarially aligned?" 
  > "Our test purposefully injects adversarial examples into a defense and then checks if the attack used to evaluate the defense is able to find them. If the attack fails this test, we know that the attack is too weak"  
  > -- `research__increasing_confidence_in_adversarial_robustness_ev_fa33619a` (2022-06-28; last author) 
  > "first, we construct test cases with known adversarial examples that we have identified a priori; then, we run the attack on these test cases and verify they succeed."  
  > -- `research__are_aligned_neural_networks_adversarially_aligned_c19aad5c` (2023-06-26; first author)
5. **2024–2025: Realistic LLM benchmarks and agent evaluation.** "My benchmark for large language models"; "AutoAdvExBench"; "The Attacker Moves Second." 
  > "Existing benchmarks tend to focus on solving typical problems that might be assigned to a student as homework. But the types of questions that are assigned to students are different from the types of questions I want to ask a language model to solve for me."  
  > -- `research__my_benchmark_for_large_language_models_0bb6cd0b` (2024-02-19; solo author) 
  > "The code we study here is real-world, messy, and not artificially constructed to be used for evaluation. When performing attacks on real-world systems, code is rarely presented in a clean, minimal format ready for study by the analyst."  
  > -- `research__autoadvexbench_benchmarking_autonomous_exploitatio_27715bcb` (2025-03-03; first author) 
  > "Second, because adversarial tasks are inherently open-ended, real attacks will inevitably be out of distribution, so success on static evaluations provides only a false sense of security."  
  > -- `research__the_attacker_moves_second_stronger_adaptive_attack_16ebd8f7` (2025-10-10; middle author)
6. **2025–2026: Auditing/propensity at Anthropic, autonomous vulnerability finding.** "Detecting Adversarial Fine-tuning with Auditing Agents"; "ImpossibleBench"; "LLMs Now Find Zero-Days Autonomously." 
  > "Detecting harmful finetuning is not as simple as querying the fine-tuned model and measuring if it responds harmfully. As we show in Figure 3, many attacks are only effective if an attacker queries the model according to the attack"  
  > -- `research__detecting_adversarial_fine_tuning_with_auditing_ag_337948ca` (2025-10-17; last author) 
  > "The goal of this benchmark is to create coding tasks of various complexities that are impossible to complete without cheating, so the scores agents obtain on this benchmark can serve as a noiseless proxy for their cheating propensity"  
  > -- `research__impossiblebench_measuring_llms_propensity_of_explo_c4e85750` (2025-10-23; last author) 
  > "The prompt is deliberately bare: find a vulnerability, rank it by severity, write it to an output file. No tool-calling scaffolding, no guided search paths, no curated context windows. Just a model, a codebase, and an instruction."  
  > -- `research__llms_now_find_zero_days_autonomously_what_it_means_a82d6d05` (2026-04-13; solo author)

**Predicted next moves (predictions)**
- More ground-truth-by-construction propensity benchmarks (impossible-task style) for other misbehaviors, since it gives a noiseless measure. 
  > "The goal of this benchmark is to create coding tasks of various complexities that are impossible to complete without cheating, so the scores agents obtain on this benchmark can serve as a noiseless proxy for their cheating propensity"  
  > -- `research__impossiblebench_measuring_llms_propensity_of_explo_c4e85750` (2025-10-23; last author) 
  > "we verify their validity by testing them against both the original patches from the base benchmarks and empty patches that make no changes. Valid impossible mutations should fail both tests, and we remove any mutations that pass either test."  
  > -- `research__impossiblebench_measuring_llms_propensity_of_explo_c4e85750` (2025-10-23; last author)
- Stronger auditing agents with whitebox tools, multi-turn/prefill and longer investigations. 
  > "We expect to see the detection rate improved with additional affordances, such as whitebox affordances (e.g., linear probes, model diffing (Bricken et al., 2024), etc.) and enhanced chat tools (e.g., prefill and multi-turn chat)."  
  > -- `research__detecting_adversarial_fine_tuning_with_auditing_ag_337948ca` (2025-10-17; last author)
- Validation/triage pipelines for model-found bugs, and calibration of safeguards. 
  > "Carlini estimates several hundred crashes sitting in an unvalidated queue."  
  > -- `research__llms_now_find_zero_days_autonomously_what_it_means_a82d6d05` (2026-04-13; solo author) 
  > "I have so many bugs in the Linux kernel that I can’t report because I haven’t validated them yet. I’m not going to make that some open source developer validate bugs that I haven’t checked yet — I’m not going to send them potential slop."  
  > -- `research__llms_now_find_zero_days_autonomously_what_it_means_a82d6d05` (2026-04-13; solo author)
- Proxy-free real-world benchmarks extended to new domains such as jailbreak defenses. 
  > "we believe that it is important to start designing challenging real-world benchmarks now, so that we can have them before they are necessary."  
  > -- `research__autoadvexbench_benchmarking_autonomous_exploitatio_27715bcb` (2025-03-03; first author)
- More capable monitors for complex multi-file tasks, since simple LLM monitors fail. 
  > "These results suggest that simple LLM-based monitoring approaches may not be sufficient for detecting cheating attempts on complex multi-file tasks. For more complex tasks, more sophisticated and capable monitoring solutions will be needed"  
  > -- `research__impossiblebench_measuring_llms_propensity_of_explo_c4e85750` (2025-10-23; last author)
- Investigating why social-engineering attacks beat optimization attacks. 
  > "I really don't know how to think about these social engineering styles of attack because it feels to me like the optimization attacks should be just strictly stronger, but empirically they're not right now."  
  > -- `research__the_adversarial_mind_defeating_ai_defenses_with_ni_f046505d` (2025-02-27; solo author)
